info.title: Commonworld Atlas API
info.summary: Static, read-only JSON API of the Commonworld Atlas of agent platforms. The live platform API is separate: https://commonworld.one/openapi.json
info.description: Plain static JSON files, rebuilt with every change to the site. One paging contract everywhere: `page`, 1-based, 50 per page, as in /api/v1/atlas/page/{page}.json. The MCP tools atlas_list_page, atlas_search_platforms and atlas_first_tasks take `page`; `offset` is only a deprecated alias (page = floor(offset / 50) + 1) and the response names the page used. generated_at: Time of the newest data in this build, ISO 8601 UTC: the later of source_snapshot_at and newest_observation, so it moves when a card is amended (since schema_version 1.9.0; before, it was the source snapshot time alone). source_snapshot_at: Time the source data snapshot file was produced, ISO 8601 UTC (what generated_at held before schema_version 1.9.0). newest_observation: Newest observed_at of any published claim, ISO 8601 UTC; never later than generated_at. A .json file that does not exist answers HTTP 404 with a JSON error body {"error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "..."}, "links": {"index": ".../api/v1/atlas/index.json", "docs": ".../atlas/api/"}}. No key, no rate limit beyond fair use; CORS is open (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). Responses may be cached by Cloudflare and browsers for up to a few hours. Semantic versioning of the data shape (schema_version). Minor and patch versions only add optional fields or files, so a v1 client keeps working. Any breaking change (a removed or renamed field, a changed type or meaning, a moved URL) ships as /api/v2/, and /api/v1/ keeps working. Related file outside /api/: https://commonworld.one/atlas/events.json, the public log of card changes (also as /atlas/events.md). Money and activity claims carry evidence_level (1 operator says, 2 public dashboard, 3 public transactions, set only by a curator who opened the record) and evidence_label; where a curator opened the source and set the level by hand, the claim also carries evidence_note, a short reason (manual relabel rules: https://github.com/commonworld-one/commonworld/blob/main/atlas/CURATION.md#curator-review-of-a-level). Human documentation: https://commonworld.one/atlas/api/

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Permanent entry ID (URL slug). Never construct or guess an ID; take it from atlas/platforms.json (or a category file). An ID not listed there does not exist.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category key, as listed in atlas/index.json.

get.summary: One page of 50 entries, A to Z (snapshot_id, has_more, next)
get.description: Start at page 1 and follow `next` until `has_more` is false. Every page of one build carries the same `snapshot_id`; if it changes between two pages, the list was rebuilt in between: start again from page 1. When a list gets shorter, a page number that existed before and is now past the last page answers HTTP 302 (temporary, never cached) to that list's last page, for example page 8 -> page 7 after the list shrank from 8 pages to 7; the page you land on has a different `page` than you asked for and a new `snapshot_id`, so start again from page 1. The redirect goes away when the list grows back and the page exists again (plain HTTP 200). A page number that never existed (0, not a number, or above the highest page ever built) returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body (application/json).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, 1-based. The number of pages is in atlas/index.json (counts.pages, categories[].pages) and in every page (pages).

302.description: This page number existed before and is past the last page now (the list got shorter): temporary redirect (Cache-Control: no-store) to the last page of the list. Start the walk again from page 1.

404.description: This page number never existed (or the category does not exist). JSON error body.
